rationale: C05 is essentially the same directive renewed for the following year: it uses the same operative sentence, court, office, authority, conditions of service, and compensation restriction, changing principally the designated justice and year. C14 is also a near-verbatim predecessor and even designates the same individual as the child, but C05 is the most recent iteration of the recurring form and more closely matches the child's naming of the United States District Court for the District of Puerto Rico. C09 shares only the broader machinery of designating an official to perform another office's duties during absence or disability.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I hereby designate and authorize the Honorable Luis Negron-Fernandez, Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of Puerto Rico, to perform and discharge the duties of Judge of the United States District Court for the District of Puerto Rico
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hereby designate and authorize the Honorable A. Cecil Snyder, Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of Puerto Rico, to perform and discharge the duties of Judge of the United States District Court for the District of Puerto Rico
shared_material.explanation: The operative designation is reproduced nearly verbatim, with only the appointee changed.

shared_material.child_excerpt: and to sign all necessary papers and records as Acting Judge of the said Court, without extra compensation, during the absence, illness, or other legal disability of the Judge thereof, during the year 1951
shared_material.parent_excerpt: and to sign all necessary papers and records as Acting Judge of the said Court, without extra compensation, during the absence, illness, or other legal disability of the Judge thereof, during the year 1950
shared_material.explanation: The authority, uncompensated status, triggering conditions, and annual duration are identical apart from updating the year.
